meta.title: Operation of Clevenger Apparatus in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To determine the volatile oil content of crude drugs by hydro-distillation using a Clevenger apparatus as per Indian Pharmacopoeia (IP) and WHO monograph requirements for essential oil-bearing crude drugs.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for quantitative determination of volatile oil in aromatic crude drugs such as clove, coriander, fennel, cardamom, eucalyptus, and peppermint.
procedure: Weigh accurately 20–50 g of coarsely powdered crude drug (as specified in the IP monograph) and place in a 1 L round-bottom flask.
Add 300–500 mL of distilled water to the flask — the drug material should be well submerged.
Add boiling chips (anti-bumping granules) to the flask.
Connect the Clevenger apparatus to the flask: attach the distillation tube to the flask neck; connect the reflux condenser on top.
Fill the graduated tube of the Clevenger apparatus with distilled water using a small funnel until water just overflows into the flask — this ensures no air pockets.
Connect the condenser cooling water supply (inlet at bottom, outlet at top) and confirm steady flow.
Heat the flask using a heating mantle (preferred) or sand bath — begin heating slowly.
Bring to a gentle boil — steam carries volatile oil vapours through the apparatus.
Condensed water and oil collect in the graduated tube: oils lighter than water float above; oils heavier than water (e.g., clove) sink below.
Maintain distillation for the time specified in the monograph (typically 3–4 hours from the first drop of distillate).
After the required time, reduce heat and allow to cool for 30 minutes.
Read the volume of oil collected in the graduated tube to the nearest 0.05 mL.
Calculate the % volatile oil content: % v/w = (Volume of oil / Weight of drug) × 100.
Compare with IP/WHO specified limits for the crude drug.
Record: drug name, weight, distillation time, volume of oil, and % content in the logbook.
Clean the Clevenger apparatus with acetone, then water; dry thoroughly before storing.
precautions: Use only distilled water — tap water mineral content interferes with measurement.
Ensure all glass joints are airtight — volatile oil losses from joints give falsely low results.
Do not heat too vigorously — violent boiling causes bumping and physical carry-over of plant material into the graduated tube.
Ensure coolant water flows throughout — stopping coolant allows uncondensed vapours to escape.
For oils denser than water: use the modified Clevenger apparatus for heavy oils or use a small volume of xylene to float the oil for reading.
Allow adequate cooling before reading the oil volume — hot oil is less dense and gives an artificially high volume reading.
Work in a well-ventilated area — aromatic vapours can cause headache with prolonged exposure.
